title: Lovie Austin's Stutz Bearcat; Hunter never owned a car; her fur cape
summary: Lovie drove too fast; Hunter never had a car and preferred buses; she paid $1,800 for a mole and seal cape.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: But now Lovie Austin used to dress in leopard skin?

She drove that Stutz. She drove that Stutz Bearcat, yeah. She wasn't so smartly dressed. Her car was smart. But she -- her clothes didn't have the fashion that Lil's had. Uh-uh, she didn't have the fashion. But she had that Stutz car, boy. She could drive it like she bought an oil field, she'd go so fast, you know. Several times I think she asked me to ride when I had some place to go; I didn't want to get in that car with Lovie, because Lovie was going too fast. I wanted to live a little longer, you know.
No, I never did have a car. Tell you why --
-- I tried, first of all I wasn't crazy about a car. I liked the transportation -- buses and things, streetcars and

I still do. I still prefer the street-cars and the buses. But I tell you what, a friend of mine tried to teach me how to drive. And everytime the lights would start coming to me, I was ready to jump out. So I knew I would either injure or kill somebody, or injure or kill myself. So I decided to give it up.

But I tell you, I had a knock-out coat. I had a furrier to make me a cape that was -- let's see, it was a -- what was the top of it? The top of it was -- what is that grey fur, not -- it wasn't squirrel. What was that grey fur?

Mole. And seal. The top of it was mole, and the bottom was seal. And it was a good seal. I paid $1,800.00 for it then, so you know it must have been all right. Had a tailor to make it. Yeah, it was all right. I finally gave it away.
